theorem_title: The Komlos-Sulyok-Szemeredi bound: a Sidon subset of size $c\sqrt{|X|}$
natural_language_statement:
For some absolute constant $c > 0$, every finite set $X$ of positive reals contains a subset $S$ with distinct pairwise sums and $|S| \ge c\sqrt{|X|}$.

Such an $S$ is a *Sidon set*: for $w, x, y, z \in S$ with $w + x = y + z$, either $w = y$ and $x = z$, or $w = z$ and $x = y$. Repeats are allowed, so $w = x$ is fine.

The constant comes before the $\forall X$, so it must handle small $X$ too, which a one-element Sidon set does. Positivity is never used, since the Sidon condition is translation invariant.
source: the lower bound half of Erdos problem 530, https://www.erdosproblems.com/530, posed by Riddell and open as stated; proved by Janos Komlos, Miklos Sulyok, and Endre Szemeredi, "Linear problems in combinatorial number theory", Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 26 (1975) 113-121; a second proof in Bailleul and Riblet, arXiv:2605.03181, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03181
